Swiss Army Bench 0.0.30

- **Your key vault's variables stay.** A vault that loads every secret now remembers its secret names (never their
  values) on this computer, so its variables are in the `${` list, on the Variables page and in notebooks from the
  moment the app opens, after a restart or an update. The names are read again in the background at start (a vault
  that would need a sign-in window is skipped quietly; its card says when the names were read, with Read again).
  Reading and saving a vault puts its variables in the `${` list straight away.
- **One name, one variable.** A name can only be given once: your own variables and a vault's named entries keep
  theirs, and a vault secret whose name is taken gets the vault's name in front (TEAM_VAULT_WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD).
  Adding or renaming to a taken name is refused in plain words.
- **Certificates from a key vault.** Trino's client certificate can come from a key vault (the form's "Client
  certificate (from a key vault)"), and any certificate setting (PostgreSQL's, MySQL's) can be a `${NAME}` from a
  vault. The certificate is used through files only you can read, removed afterwards, and never stored; no "Only
  works on your machine" note.
- **Dataverse's SQL endpoint:** a SQL Server connection on it now lists its tables (the endpoint refuses part of
  SQL Server's language, so a plainer listing is used).
